answer:
Keep Python, but revise the integration boundary. The project’s Python-only constraint takes precedence, and mytech explicitly favors implementing application-specific HTTP adapters in the application’s language. There is no reason here to introduce Rust or another runtime. [Guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/external-http/rust-for-external-http-protocols.md)

Move provider-response decoding and validation into a narrow Python client or adapter. Route handlers should translate inbound requests, invoke the reporting operation, and map its results to HTTP responses. Keep deterministic report transformations in pure functions consuming validated, project-owned values. This can remain a few modules in one service. [Boundary guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/boundary-owned-contracts-and-pure-cores.md)

Replace raw upstream error strings with stable project-owned error categories and sanitized messages. Upstream wording is an unstable caller contract and may expose sensitive details; callers should not need to parse it to decide recovery. The adapter should also own timeouts, safe retry policy, and response-size bounds. [HTTP guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/external-http/external-http-contracts-and-handwritten-clients.md)

For this application-local integration, executable response schemas and independently authored provider examples may suffice; OpenAPI is not automatically necessary. Verify malformed responses, upstream failures, timeouts, retry behavior, and redaction through the transport boundary. The supplied description provides no provider evidence, so protocol specifics remain unknown.
